week.weeklyOverview: Play-based STEM week: children predict, build, test, and talk about what happened—towers, bridges, ramps, sink-or-float, and marble runs. No elementary worksheets. Teachers narrate scientific language while protecting inquiry joy. Document children’s words and photos of setups; celebrate redesign after “flops.”
week.weeklyMaterials: Unit blocks and loose parts; paper cups; craft sticks; tape; cardboard for ramps; water table or tubs; sink/float objects; measuring cups/rulers; magnifying glasses; clipboards for blueprint drawing; play dough; large soft balls for movement STEM; marble-run tubes and marbles only with strict safety protocol (or substitute large pom-poms/balls for mixed-age); dominoes; smocks; towels.
week.teacherPreparation: Stage centers before arrival and preview one open-ended STEM invitation; step back so children lead.
week.familyConnection: We are STEM explorers—asking questions, building, and testing ideas. At home try: “What might happen if…?” with blocks, water play, or cardboard ramps. Celebrate trying again more than getting it “right.”
milestones: Language: Uses STEM talk—predict, observe, test, compare, redesign.
SEL: Persists after structures fall; collaborates on team builds; shares materials.
Cognition: Makes predictions; compares results; notices patterns and cause/effect on ramps.
Motor: Stacks/balances; pours at water table; controls drawing tools for blueprints.
Creativity: Invents original structures and marble/ramp pathways through open-ended design.

printableIdeas.title: Predict / Observe Mini Chart (Picture)
printableIdeas.purpose: Two-column picture chart for Sink or Float and Ramp Testing—children mark guesses with stamps/X, then results; not a graded worksheet.

printableIdeas.title: Blueprint Paper (Blank Grid Light)
printableIdeas.purpose: Light grid for Blueprint Drawing / Engineer Showcase planning; scribbles and dictation welcome.

printableIdeas.title: STEM Challenge Cards
printableIdeas.purpose: Simple picture challenges (“build a bridge for a toy car,” “make a ramp”) for STEM Exploration Stations.

songs.title: Predict, Test, Learn (LLH STEM Chant)
songs.motions: Finger to temple on predict; hands push gently on test; hands as binoculars on observe; rolling hands on redesign.
songs.teacherDirections: Teach on Monday before Scientist Investigation Station. Use the chant whenever a tower falls—normalize redesign.
songs.whenToUse: Before any experiment or build challenge.
songs.suggestedPace: Clear, medium pace; clap on “another turn.”
songs.transitionPurpose: Installs inquiry cycle language without worksheets.
songs.lyrics:
Predict, predict—what might we see?
Test, test—try carefully.
Observe, observe—look and learn,
Then redesign for another turn!

Builders build and scientists say:
“What happened? Why?”—we learn that way.

songs.title: Build It Up, Build It Strong (LLH)
songs.motions: Wide hands for base; stacking motions; dramatic tip-over then calm rebuild gestures.
songs.teacherDirections: Pair with Build the Tallest Tower and Bridge Builders. Praise wide bases and teamwork, not only height.
songs.whenToUse: Block center open; engineer showcase warm-up.
songs.transitionPurpose: Focuses children on stable design strategies.
songs.lyrics:
Build it up, build it strong,
Base is wide and it lasts long.
Stack it high, then watch it go—
If it falls we rebuild slow.

One more block, one more try,
Engineers ask how and why!

songs.title: Roll, Roll, Ramp (LLH)
songs.motions: Diagonal arm as ramp; finger “ball” rolling down; arms wide for safe space.
songs.teacherDirections: Use before Ramp Testing / Marble Run Challenge. Practice the safety line “give space to try” with bodies first—no marbles until spacing is clear.
songs.whenToUse: Ramp and marble-run days; outdoor ball-ramp play.
songs.suggestedPace: Upbeat but stop fully on safety line.
songs.transitionPurpose: Connects motion science with safety routines.
songs.lyrics:
Roll, roll, ramp—ready, set, go!
High or low—what do we know?
Fast or slow, we watch it race,
Science smiles on every face.

Move back please—give space to try,
Safe scientists standing by!

songs.title: Sink or Float Song (LLH)
songs.motions: Thumbs down for sink, palms up for float; drop motion; binocular eyes.
songs.teacherDirections: Sing at the water table before Sink or Float Experiment. Record predictions on a simple chart with pictures—not a worksheet packet.
songs.whenToUse: Water table STEM; Tuesday science focus.
songs.suggestedPace: Playful; pause for each object prediction.
songs.transitionPurpose: Frames prediction talk before water exploration.
songs.lyrics:
Will it sink? Will it float?
Make a guess, then test the boat!
In the water, watch and see—
Science friends investigate with me.

books.title: Rosie Revere, Engineer
books.author: Andrea Beaty
books.whyThisBook: Celebrates prototyping and persistence after failed inventions—perfect for tower/bridge redesign culture.
beforeReadingQuestions: Have you ever built something that fell down? What did you try next?
duringReadingPrompts: How is Rosie feeling when her invention flops?
afterReadingQuestions: What will we say in our classroom when a build falls?
What invention do you want to test today?
books.substituteTitle: Iggy Peck, Architect by Andrea Beaty

books.title: Ada Twist, Scientist
books.author: Andrea Beaty
books.whyThisBook: Models question-asking and investigation—pairs with Scientist Investigation Station and journals as drawing, not worksheets.
beforeReadingQuestions: What is something you wonder about?
duringReadingPrompts: What is Ada trying to figure out?
afterReadingQuestions: What question will you investigate at our STEM stations?
How can we record what we notice (draw, photo, dictate)?
books.substituteTitle: What Is Science? by Rebecca Kai Dotlich

books.title: What Do You Do With an Idea?
books.author: Kobi Yamada
books.whyThisBook: Supports inventive thinking and confidence—nice bridge to Inventor Dramatic Play and Engineer Showcase.
beforeReadingQuestions: What idea might you build with today?
duringReadingPrompts: How does the child treat the idea at first?
What changes as the idea grows?
afterReadingQuestions: How will we take care of each other’s ideas in the makerspace?
What materials could help your idea?
books.substituteTitle: Not a Box by Antoinette Portis

teacherToolkit.teacherPreparation: Stage centers before arrival and preview one open-ended STEM invitation; step back so children lead.
prepChecklist: Set materials at child height before arrival
Place cleanup caddy near the play space
Review allergy and supervision notes for the day
observationFocus: Persists with a material or peer exchange
Shows interest or curiosity during invitations
observationPrompts: What language or gestures appear during play?
How does the child enter and leave the invitation?
Where do peers support or extend the idea?
documentationPrompts: Capture one moment of child-led exploration (with permission).
Note a verbatim quote or gesture tied to the theme.
teacherTips: Model once, then narrate what you notice.
Offer two choices instead of open-ended demands.
Keep transitions short with a familiar song cue.
setupCleanupShortcuts: Trays labeled and stacked by day
Damp cloth + bin for quick reset
Spare substitution basket on the shelf

materialSubstitutions.use: printed picture cards or recycled clean containers

teacherToolkit.mixedAgeAdaptations: Offer a simpler parallel tray for younger friends and a design challenge for older preschoolers.
teacherToolkit.extraSupportAdaptations: Sit beside, shorten the invitation, and offer hand-under-hand only when welcomed.
teacherToolkit.challengeExtensions: Invite children to invent a new STEM rule, map, or story for peers.
teacherToolkit.safetyInclusionNotes: Play-based inquiry only—avoid worksheet packets. Marble runs: use only with preschoolers who do not mouth objects; establish a “marble zone” with clear floor space, eye protection from flying pieces not required but keep rolls aimed at walls/trays not walkways; count marbles in/out; substitute large pom-poms, ping-pong balls, or cars for mixed-age or mouthing children. Water table: mop slips, limit depth, no standing water left unattended. Towers: soft fall zones; no climbing builds. Dominoes and small STEM bits stored up when toddlers visit. Tape dispensers adult-managed.
teacherToolkit.endOfWeekReflection: Which STEM words and strategies showed up most in play?
teacherToolkit.familyConnection: Share one STEM word or song to try at home during ordinary routines.
